verbs.summary: Open-ended live streams both ways with a peer that follows its mailbox; nothing is stored.

verbs.usage: send <target> [--id ID] [--subject VERB] [--size N] [--wait S] [--durable] (-- <message> | -m | -m:rfc5322 | --file NAME) [--chunked] [--live]
verbs.summary: Send a message or a file; --live offers it to a live recipient and returns its reply.
Send a tar on stdin as one message, stored as received.
List, read or follow a mailbox as a chunked stream; only a read without --peek consumes.
Stream a bag back as the tar it came as; consumes it without --peek.
Drop handled messages and notices; -m:ids reads the ids from stdin, one per line; --before[-including] drops what precedes an id in listing order.
Take a live exchange announced on your follow.
Subscribe to a topic; prints the subscription's name.
Drop a subscription and its mailbox.
As an address that takes instances: bind an instance to the key on stdin.
Drop one of your instances; as an instance, yourself.
As an address that takes instances: admit instances as targets, answering their ask.
As an address that takes instances: say an instance does not exist: its claim and mailbox go.
List your instances: mail waiting, holder, claim.
List reachable targets and their types.
What the hub supports, or what an address handles.
Register what this identity handles, checked by the hub.
